_comment: XRAS stress scenarios. Mirrors tests/perf/baselines.json in shape and role.
The organising principle is NOT 'stress the handlers'. It is:
stress the handlers and assert on the AUDIT ROW.
Every scenario declares what `xras_action_log` must say afterwards, because
that row is the only artefact that survives into triage week. Cutover is an
abrupt repoint with no observation window: if an operator cannot answer a
question from the row alone, the answer is a missing column — and the DBA
ticket is still unfiled, which is the last cheap window to learn that.
Each entry:
what        — one line, what is being pushed
expect      — the terminal audit-row state: received|processed|manual|failed
http        — the status code the route answers
triage      — the operator question this scenario answers FROM THE ROW
verdict     — 'answered' when the row suffices; otherwise the column that
would be needed. A 'verdict' that names a column is schema
evidence, NOT a failing test.
Run:  pytest -m stress -n 0
-n 0 is deliberate in the docs but not enforced: these write audit rows on
their own connection, and the `action_log` fixture deletes by captured PK
precisely so they are xdist-safe. See tests/xras_audit.py.

oversize_error_messages.what: 1000 resources on a New, each with an unmapped key AND a bad amount
oversize_error_messages.triage: Did the audit write survive an error list larger than the column?
notes: Under STRICT_TRANS_TABLES (confirmed on) an oversized value does not
truncate, it RAISES — losing the audit row entirely, which is the one
failure this table cannot afford.
WHICH PATH reaches the condition was the useful finding, and it moved
once the resource key field name was corrected:
Supplement  1.00x  — a failed key resolution `continue`s before the
amount is read, so one message per resource,
against an entry of almost identical length.
NOT reachable: the body hits its limit first.
New         1.79x  — `_plan_allocations` calls resolve_resource AND
transaction_amount unconditionally, so one
resource yields TWO messages. Measured 59,090
bytes of body producing 105,999 of messages.
So the guard sits on the only path that can reach it. A `resources[]`
field name shorter than `resourceRepositoryKey` would change this.

oversize_raw_payload.what: a POST body larger than the raw_payload column
oversize_raw_payload.triage: Does an oversized body still leave a row behind?
notes: The action is REFUSED, not applied: a body we cannot record is one we
cannot audit or replay, so processing it would write allocations against
a record that does not survive. 422 rather than 413 because the error
list is what XRAS's own panel renders.
`raw_payload` is TEXT NOT NULL and was written unguarded, at the FIRST
write, before dispatch. An oversized body therefore lost the row before
anything else could go wrong.
Largest observed corpus payload is 4,819 bytes — ~13x headroom — so this
is a tail risk rather than a live one. It is guarded anyway because the
cost of being wrong is the whole audit trail for that action.

repeat_post_supplement.what: the same Supplement posted three times
repeat_post_supplement.triage: Is this the same action I saw an hour ago?
repeat_post_supplement.verdict: answered — action_id landed; this now proves detection
notes: Supplement is ADDITIVE: three posts of 250,000 leave 750,000. That is
correct per-post behaviour and the wrong total.
Three rows were identical in every column an operator can filter on;
`actionId` lived only as bytes inside `raw_payload`, so detecting the
duplicate meant parsing JSON out of a TEXT column.
RESOLVED: `action_id` is an indexed column. XRAS still owns the retry —
this was always about DETECTION, which no later code change could add
without a second DBA ticket.
Extension is near-idempotent, via the equal-end-date skip alone: the
second post finds every account already at the requested end and writes
nothing. The blast radius of a double-post is therefore zero HERE and
not zero for Supplement — which is the asymmetry worth knowing before
cutover, since Extension is 60% of traffic and Supplement is 15%.
One of FOUR parking causes that produce byte-identical rows: nothing
matched, the type is disabled by XRAS_ACTIONS_ENABLED, no handler is
registered, or Transfer parked by design.
`DispatchResult` has carried `service` and `reason` since Sprint C and
the route logged them; k8s app logs are ephemeral, so within days the row
was all that was left and it could not tell the four apart.
RESOLVED: both are columns now. A NULL `service` is itself the answer for
this cause — no service was ever selected.

park_disabled_type.what: a type disabled by the XRAS_ACTIONS_ENABLED triage lever
park_disabled_type.triage: Did my 3am config change park this, or did it never match?
notes: The lever exists to park a misbehaving payload class by config instead
of by revert. An operator who pulls it and then cannot confirm from the
table that it took effect is flying blind during the incident it exists
for.

park_transfer_by_design.what: Transfer, which is deliberately not serviced
notes: The ONLY one of the four parking causes with an in-table discriminator,
and only because Transfer has a dedicated action_type.
`projcode_result` carries the projcode on the manual arm (C.1a) and
`outcome_reason` now carries NOT_IMPLEMENTED_REASON — the sentence
written specifically for whoever reads this row at 3am.

unsampled_renewal.what: actionType 'Renewal' — declared on the wire, never sampled
unsampled_renewal.triage: Does a wire type we have never seen route correctly?
notes: Shares the Update path with New-against-an-existing-project. Zero
instances in the 175 measured posts and none in the corpus, so this is
the first time the code has seen one.
MEASURED: it reaches UpdateHandler and returns six real error strings —
Missing title / Missing pi role / No FieldOfScience (fos) objects /
Unable to determine allocation type from action data / Missing begin
date for allocation(s) / Missing end date for allocation(s).
'failed' is the CORRECT outcome for a minimal payload; the claim being
made is that an unsampled type produces a reviewable 422 rather than a
500 or a silent park. Legacy answers an opaque 500 here.

unsampled_advance.what: actionType 'Advance' — declared, with no legacy service
unsampled_advance.triage: Confirm it parks rather than erroring, and that the row says so
notes: Legacy has no AdvanceProjectActionService at all, so it falls off the
end of the selector chain. Parking is correct; being indistinguishable
from the other three parks is not.

copi_role_spelling.what: 'Co-PI' and 'CoPi' — the spelling is still unknown
copi_role_spelling.triage: Does an unknown roleType spelling break the roster?
notes: The roster ignores roleType entirely when building MEMBERSHIP — it takes
every username in roles[] — so both spellings survive. The risk was only
ever on role ASSIGNMENT, where only 'PI' and 'Allocation Manager' are
matched and anything else is simply not a candidate.
This closes a question the corpus could not: hdt@ucar.edu has not sent a
sample and production capture only starts at cutover.
